state.case_summary:
A 27-year-old man with a history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck treated six years earlier by wide local excision (no sentinel lymph node biopsy, no adjuvant therapy) presented with hemoptysis and dyspnea. Vital signs were within normal limits. Physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor. Laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were unremarkable.

Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe. Endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor. Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET). 

Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone. Ultrasound–guided core needle biopsy of the hyoid lesion was nondiagnostic, yielding only rare atypical epithelial cells amidst lymphocytes.

A multidisciplinary sarcoma tumor board concluded that the hyoid lesion most likely represented a synchronous primary bone tumor (e.g., plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, or osteosarcoma). Given his pulmonary symptoms and the potential for chemotherapy to treat both lesions, he received 14 cycles of vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, and etoposide (VCD/IE). 

Mid-treatment PET/CT demonstrated a substantial decrease in size and complete metabolic response of the lung mass but development of right neck adenopathy and interval growth of the hyoid bone lesion, suggesting a distinct pathology.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. melanoma
B. Metastatic Ewing sarcoma/PNET was initially considered given the lung tumor’s pathology and synchronous hyoid lesion
C. Primary hyoid bone tumors such as plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, and osteosarcoma were considered based on imaging
D. Metastatic melanoma was confirmed by the tumor’s melanocytic immunoprofile, including positivity for S
E. None
F. None
G. None
H. None
